label: rem:archimedean-image-table
title: Per-structure action of the archimedean realisation $\tau$
html:
The fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch}, followed by the archimedean evaluation \pi_\infty \colon \mathrm{Obj}(\mathbf{Arch}) \to \mathbb{R} (def:archimedean-realization-functor), maps each algebraic structure on the categorical side to a concrete real-valued object at the substrate parameter q_0. (Per the notation register, \tau is the functor; the archimedean realization \pi_\infty \circ \tau is an evaluation into \mathbb{R}, not itself a functor between QOU categories.) The table below catalogues these images systematically, distinguishing structures that are implemented in the current pipeline from those that remain open infrastructure targets.

The organising principle: every row is a functorial image. Where the image is a scalar, it enters the mass formula directly. Where the image is a richer object (polynomial, matrix, family), it carries structural data beyond what any single scalar evaluation can access. The HOMFLYPT family (row 5) is the first non-trivial example: it simultaneously encodes the quantum \mathrm{SU}(N) invariant for every rank N, and its polynomial coefficients (integers, q-independent) survive the functor as categorical constants.

See Table 1.

Reading the table. Rows 1--4 and 7--9 form the implemented derivation chain: categorical data enters as a braid (row 1), is represented in the Hecke algebra (row 2), traced via the Markov trace (row 3 = row 4 at N = 2), decomposed through Wedderburn / Frobenius (rows 7--8), and optimised via LP/SDP (row 9). Every step is implemented and produces a real observable at q_0.

The duality column. Each algebraic structure admits a natural dual that pairs with it under a specific duality type. The physically deepest entries are:

  • Row 2 (Hopf antipode). The Hecke antipode S(T_w) = T_{w^{-1}} is the algebraic expression of crossing reversal. Under \tau, this is the structural mechanism behind the proton/neutron mass split: the proton and neutron braids \beta_p, \beta_n differ by crossing signs, and S is the map between them. The \tau-image of S is the real-valued gap \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_n) - \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_p), which (after calibration) gives \mathfrak{Q}_\beta.

  • Row 5 (HOMFLYPT mirror). The mirror P(\bar K) = P(K; a^{-1}, z) simultaneously encodes chirality for every SU(N) channel. This is the multi-N generalisation of CPT in row 4 (Jones mirror): where row 4 gives matter/antimatter at N = 2, row 5 gives matter/antimatter at every representation-theoretic rank.

  • Row 9 (LP strong duality). The primal/dual pair (x, y^*) in the operator-selection LP is already central to the mass formula: y^* are the binding-energy shadow prices, and strong duality guarantees that \sum t_i x_i^* = n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^*. The duality here is self-contained — both sides live at the same q_0 — whereas rows 2 and 5 are dualities that pair different physical states (proton/neutron, particle/antiparticle).

Row 5 (HOMFLYPT) is the highest-value open infrastructure target: it gives the entire N-indexed family in a single computation, where the current pipeline accesses only the N = 2 slice. The polynomial coefficients are integers (q-independent), so they sit on the correct axis for structural derivations that the reframing in identified: constants from substrate, not q-dependent coincidences.

The HOMFLYPT specialisation family. For a braid closure \hat\beta with HOMFLYPT polynomial P(\hat\beta; a, z) \in \mathbb{Z}[a^{\pm 1}, z^{\pm 1}]:

  P(\hat\beta;\, q_0^{N-1},\, q_0 - q_0^{-1})
  \;=\;
  \text{quantum } \mathrm{SU}(N) \text{ invariant of } \hat\beta
  \qquad (N = 2, 3, 4, \ldots)

See Table 2.

Each row is a different functor image of the same categorical object P(K), evaluated at a different representation-theoretic point. The mass tower may use different N-slices for different particles — this is not constrained by the current pipeline, which accesses only N = 2.
